chapters.title: CHAPTER 1 — ARRIVAL
chapters.subtitle: $30,000. A laptop. A phone. A city.

objectives.text: Read your notifications (Tab)
Head outside and look around Riverside
Grab a coffee at Bloom Coffee
Visit Nexus Co-work in Startup Hub (walk east)
Check the Business Board and pick a first business

on_complete.text: Ecommerce? Like... selling stuff online?
Buy low. Sell less low. Got it, haha.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 2 — FIRST CUSTOMER
chapters.subtitle: Earn your first dollar.

objectives.text: Buy your first stock (Company OS → Operations). Laptop at home or a co-work desk.
Wait for your stock to arrive: work a part-time shift meanwhile, and sleep at night
Photograph your product and list it on ShopLane (Company OS → Sales)
Wait for your first order
Pack the order at your packing table, then ship it
Get the parcel delivered to your customer

on_complete.text: Wait. Someone actually bought one??
First revenue! ShopLane pays out on Mondays.

objectives.text: Deal with an unhappy customer (check your phone)

chapters.title: CHAPTER 3 — OPEN FOR BUSINESS
chapters.subtitle: Make it official. Or don't.

objectives.text: Register your company at City Hall (Civic Center, take the Metro)

on_start.text: If this is real, make it real. City Hall does registrations. Civic Center.
FYI personal seller accounts cap out at $2,500/month on ShopLane. Registered businesses don't.

objectives.text: Open a business account for {company} at Nexus Bank (Financial District)
Decide where {company} works: home, a co-work desk, or Suite 2B (Startup Hub)
Sit down at your desk and open Company OS as {company}

on_complete.text: Look at you. A whole company. Drinks on {company}?

chapters.title: CHAPTER 4 — GROWING PAINS
chapters.subtitle: Too many orders. Not enough hours.

objectives.text: Register {company} as an employer (City Hall permits kiosk, Civic Center)

on_start.text: You packed boxes until 1 AM again, didn't you. You need help. Like, a person.

objectives.text: Post your first job ad (Company OS → People)
Hire your first employee (applicants reply within a day)
Make your first payroll: keep cash in the company for Friday 17:00
Revenue isn't cash: check the cash forecast (Company OS → Finance)

on_complete.text: A payroll. You're somebody's boss now. That's terrifying. Proud of you.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 5 — THE BIG CONTRACT
chapters.subtitle: Daniel buys by the pallet.

objectives.text: Meet Daniel Wong at Nexus Co-work (Thursdays 17:00–20:00)

on_start.text: Daniel Wong, Crestline. You're doing real volume now. Let's talk. Nexus Co-work, Thursday after 5.

objectives.text: Crestline's offer is in Company OS → Contracts: accept, counter or decline
Get 800 desk lamps in stock or on the way (cash, supplier terms, a Nexus Bank loan or an investor)
objectives.skip_text: The Crestline deal will not go ahead. Carry on with your next venture.

objectives.text: Deliver Crestline's lamps before the deadline (Company OS → Contracts)
objectives.skip_text: The Crestline deal will not go ahead. Carry on with your next venture.

on_complete.text: Received. Accounts payable will process your invoice. Net 60, as agreed.
The big deal didn't go ahead. Growth that kills you isn't growth.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 6 — CASH IS OXYGEN
chapters.subtitle: Profit on paper. Payroll on Friday.

objectives.text: Check the cash forecast: does {company} make it to the next big payment?

on_start.text: Marcus Reed here. Big invoices on long terms are how profitable companies run out of cash. My door's open, weekdays 1 to 4.

objectives.text: Bridge the gap: a bank loan, an investor, cutting costs or early payment
Collect the money Crestline owes you
objectives.skip_text: The Crestline deal will not go ahead. Carry on with your next venture.

objectives.text: Close a month with cash in the bank, or review two month-ends with negative cash

on_complete.text: You survived the cash crunch. Most people don't even know they're in one.
Came through the cash crunch.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 7 — SUPPLY SHOCK
chapters.subtitle: The boxes are stuck at sea.

objectives.text: Something's wrong with shipping: read the news board at Bloom Coffee

on_start.text: Heads up. Container rates just doubled and the port's backed up. Lead times are going to get ugly.

objectives.text: Talk to Ken about supply (Nexus Co-work, Tue and Thu 10–15), or wait for his call
Keep {company} stocked through the shock: 100 units in hand or on the way
Costs went up: raise a price to protect your margin (Company OS → Sales)
Close a month through the shock: make a profit, or review two losing months

on_complete.text: You kept the shelves full while half the city ran out. That's a real business.
Came through the Supply Shock.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 8 — THE GREEN SHIFT
chapters.subtitle: Aurelia goes electric.

objectives.text: The city passed the Clean Packaging Act: read the news board

on_start.text: Heads up for sellers: plastic-padded parcels now pay a $0.40 levy. The Green Business Grant opened too. Ask at the permits kiosk.

objectives.text: Switch to recycled packaging (Company OS → Operations)
Add a green product: buy Verdant Supply's solar desk lamps and list them

on_start.text: Verdant Supply just opened in the Industrial Zone. Their solar desk lamps are all over ShopLane.

objectives.text: Apply for the Green Business Grant at the City Hall permits kiosk

on_complete.text: Green AND profitable? Who even are you.
Went green with the city.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 9 — CLEARING CRISIS
chapters.subtitle: The payment still hasn't landed.

objectives.text: Cross-border payments are jammed: read the news board

on_start.text: Marcus Reed. Wires abroad are taking a week or more to clear. If you import, talk to Lina Zhao on our trade desk, weekdays 10 to 4.

objectives.text: Order from Lumina Direct: factory prices, but you pay before it ships
The payment is stuck: talk to Lina Zhao at Nexus Bank (weekdays 10–16)
Get the payment through: wait for the wire, or speed it up (Company OS → Operations)
Receive the import from Lumina Direct

on_complete.text: Payment landed, boxes arrived. Remember who held your money in between. That's this year's lesson.
Got an import through the Clearing Crisis.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 10 — DIGITAL RAILS
chapters.subtitle: Money that moves when the goods do.

objectives.text: Digital finance is booming: read the news board at Bloom Coffee

on_start.text: Lina Zhao. We launched something for importers: escrow on delivery. It's optional. Come by Nexus Bank, weekdays 10 to 4, and I'll show you.
Heard Lina's got a new way to pay Lumina. Worth a look. She doesn't oversell.

objectives.text: Lina Zhao has an offer for importers: talk to her at Nexus Bank (weekdays 10–16), or wait for her call
Import from Lumina Direct: pay with escrow, or the traditional way (Company OS → Operations)
Get the import delivered

on_complete.text: Goods arrived, escrow released, and nobody had to trust anybody's promise. That's the whole product. It also runs on software, so keep that in mind.
Wire, letter of credit, whatever fits. The escrow offer stands whenever you want it.
Look at you, comparing payment rails. Whatever happened to 'I just want to sell phone stands'?
Tried the new payment rails.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 11 — THE OTHER SIDE OF TRUST
chapters.subtitle: We solved one trust problem and created another.

objectives.text: Digital dollars are everywhere now: read the news board at Bloom Coffee

on_start.text: Lina Zhao. Volumes tripled since spring. Every importer I know is on the rails now. Enjoy the quiet.
Marcus Reed. Fast isn't the same as safe. Keep a wire route warm.

objectives.text: Restock from Lumina Direct before the rush: pay the way that suits you (Company OS → Operations)
Get through the freeze: the digital-dollar rail is closed for about a week (watch your phone)
Restock {company}: get the Lumina import delivered

on_complete.text: We solved one trust problem and created another. Now you've seen it from the inside. The rail is still useful. It just isn't magic.
Money that's stuck feels different from money that's gone. Glad you made it through.
Came through the bridge exploit.

chapters.title: CHAPTER 12 — REGULATION & SCALE
chapters.subtitle: Growing up means paperwork.

objectives.text: New rules for big payments and imports: read the news board at Bloom Coffee

on_start.text: Ana at City Hall. The Payments Integrity Act is in force. Commercial importers need an import licence: $450 a year, at the permits kiosk. There's a monthly compliance cost now too.
Local suppliers are untouched. It's the imports that need the paperwork. Lumina especially.

objectives.text: Get an import licence at the City Hall permits kiosk
Import in bulk: a payment over $2,500 goes through a KYC check (Company OS → Operations)
Victor Hale has read your numbers: meet him at Crestline (weekdays 11–16), or wait for his call

on_start.text: Victor Hale. I'd like to talk about {company}. I'm at the Crestline flagship on weekdays, eleven to four. If that's inconvenient, I'll call.

on_complete.title: ENDING — A NEW OWNER
on_complete.subtitle: You built {company} and sold it well. The desk is still yours.

on_complete.title: ENDING — ON YOUR TERMS
on_complete.subtitle: A better price, a longer handshake. A year to earn the rest.

on_complete.text: You turned a laptop and $30,000 into something a stranger wants to buy. Whatever you told Victor, I'm proud of you.
Season one ends here. The next market is overseas.
